title: Tools shell manifest
description: One manifest per tool, as a classic self-registering script: manifest.js calls Shell.registerManifest({...}) with this object. There is no fetch anywhere in the shipped shell, because under file:// a classic <script src> is the only mechanism that loads external data. Adding a chapter, lens, example or style is an edit to this file plus a folder drop; the deploy is a folder copy. scripts/build-site.mjs validates every manifest against this schema in a vm sandbox and fails the build on a violation.

id.description: Must equal the tool's folder name.

mode.description: course = ordered and pedagogical; prev/next is primary; the landing route is the first entry. catalogue = lateral and comparative; the landing route is the contact sheet.

adapter.description: The tool's DEFAULT lane. An entry or an example may override it — see `lane`.

runtime.description: Path to the adapter script, relative to the tool folder. Informational: the page loads its adapters with ordinary <script src> tags.

siblings.description: The tool switcher. The same list in every tool's manifest.

vocabulary.description: Editorial vocabulary, declared so the shell can render definitions rather than bare words.

sections.description: Level 1 of the nav. The rail's group order follows this array.

styles.description: A style is a set of entries sharing a palette, type and texture system. Declared once; entries point at it by id. The shell renders #/style/<id> as the declaration followed by a filtered contact sheet.

entries.description: Level 2 of the nav, in order. An item is EITHER a slug — meaning the entry registers itself from content/<slug>/entry.js, which the shell injects as a classic script — OR a complete entry object given inline, for the six-line entry that does not need a folder. Both forms may be mixed. entries.length is the only source of any count anywhere on any page. An encyclopedia manifest may ship empty at ck-e0 — the front door then renders as a page that says so.

skills.description: The fourteen skills that produce, critique or govern work in this archive. Only competency rungs get their own pages — an unbuilt rung is rendered empty, on purpose. An entity declares which skills touch it with `governed_by: [<skill-id>, ...]`; the shell resolves those against this list at ck-e8, and build-site.mjs fails the deploy on an unresolvable id.

redirects.description: Old routes that resolve to a new hash in this manifest. ck-e1 uses this so a link to the pre-fold #/kls01-ki-landscape lands on the merged W1 exploration and a link to #/13-fbm lands on the fBm technique. Keys are old hash paths (without the leading #/); values are new hash paths (with #/).

lane.description: PLAN §5.2: the lane is per entry and per example, not per tool. `audio` was added at ck-e0 (see team2/sound/SOUND-SECTION.md and REVIEW-SOUND.md §2.6): sound is a lane, not a parallel encyclopedia.

isolation.description: iframe is the only supported value for HTML fragments; shadow DOM cannot resolve url(#id) filter references and scoped prefixes leak. See ux/02-manifest-schema.md §5.

status.description: Editorial standing, not build state. PLAN §2.7 adds known-failure: the tools ship graded failures from Julia's own repos as teaching material, and filing one as `exploration` would be a lie. ck-e0 adds `unsorted` for the 74-row inventory import that lands without a ruling — visible in `#/unfiled`, counted at the front door. `stub` is a separate boolean flag rendered as a mark, so the chip row stays one line, and `technical_reference` is a tag.

entity.description: The five kinds of thing this archive holds (DOMAIN-MODEL §1). A technique is a verb with a lesson; an atom is a noun with parameters; a style is a bounded house; an exploration is a dated artefact; a coupling is an exploration that declares a `driver` and a `consequences[]` table (REVIEW-SOUND §2.2 — no new page-kind). Defaults to `exploration` on any entry that omits it, which is what every currently-shipped lens or chapter is.

atom_kind.description: The eleven kinds an atom can be (DOMAIN-MODEL §1.2, RECOMMENDATION §5.3). Substrate, process and texture are siblings in that order — the answer to Julia's TEXTURE question rendered as column order rather than argued in a paragraph (DOMAIN-MODEL §4). `voice`, `space`, `bus` are the audio siblings of visual atoms and sit in the same grid.

relation_kind.description: Relations declared on ONE side of an entry pair. scripts/index-tools.mjs --mirror writes the back-link, so a broken back-link is not something a human can create by hand. Six were shipped before ck-e0; three are added here: `sound-behind` is the mirror of `shader-behind` for the audio lane; `shared-cause` is the audio review's replacement for a parallel-vocabulary edge (REVIEW-SOUND §2.6); `ancestor-of` is the removal-test-with-a-URL edge (DOMAIN-MODEL §2.1). `overuses` is the symptoms relation (an entry that overuses an atom points at that atom).

source.description: Attribution. Required on anything not written here from scratch.

kind.description: original = written for this tool. adapted = derived from a named source. reference-study = a rebuild of someone else's designed artefact. own-work = a shipped ø / client piece. quoted = reproduced verbatim under licence.

related.description: Cross-tool and in-tool links. Declared on ONE side; scripts/index-tools.mjs --mirror writes the back-link, so a broken back-link is not something a human can create by hand.

tool.description: Omit for a link inside this tool.

param.description: A named knob, bound as a uniform (glsl) or as a key of `p` (canvas2d). Deliberately capped at 3 per example: a knob is an editorial decision and the default is zero knobs.

example.description: Level 3 of the nav. Examples live in a strip under the stage, never in the rail — which is what lets one chapter carry 23 upstream .frag files without wrecking the index.

lane.description: Overrides the entry's lane for this example.

file.description: The file of record beside the entry (main.frag, main.js). Not loaded at runtime — file:// forbids it — but it is what scripts/index-tools.mjs --mirror copies into `code`, and what the apparatus prints as the path.

code.description: The source, inline. This is what actually runs.

fragment.description: HTML fragment document, relative to the entry path (fragment lane).

thumb.description: A filename, or a filename plus an authored crop. PLAN §2.7: the contact-sheet crop is a picture editor's decision, not a computed one.

crop.description: [scale, offsetY, offsetX?]. scale is a MULTIPLE of fit-to-card — 1 shows the whole plate width, 1.4 is a 1.4x detail — so a card that changes width when the rail closes does not change what the crop means. offsetY is the design-pixel row that lands at the top of the card; offsetX, optional and 0 by default, is the column that lands at its left edge. The rectangle the three of them cut must be the card's own ratio, 232:196, which build-site.mjs checks: a plate shorter than designWidth*196/232 has to be cropped INTO, and a zoom anchored at x=0 cuts the last letter off a centred wordmark.

type.description: The three type roles. A fragment in this style links content/_styles/<id>.css, which is where these families and any @font-face actually live — PLAN §5.11.

engines.description: Shared engine scripts the style's fragments include — the machine-readable form of 'reuse, don't redefine'.

rules.description: The non-negotiables for this style, in Julia's words. Printed on the style page, next to the work they govern.

entries.description: Optional and derivable: entries also declare their style.

exercise.description: One rung of the ladder. research/04 §2(d): the book's exercises escalate and the playground kept only the bottom rung. Rungs 3 and 4 are where a shader stops being a demo and becomes a composition.

stage_step.description: One step of the build-up — codeAndCanvas used as a SEQUENCE, which is the move the book makes and the playground flattened into a destination.

default.description: The step the entry opens on. At most one.

variant.description: One member of a family, shown side by side and loaded into the stage on click — the glslGallery move, restored.

plot.description: The 1-D function plotter — simpleFunction, restored. It isolates the shape of a value from everything else, which is the purest statement of 'control comes from shaping values, not selecting effects'. `expr` is evaluated by learn/plot.js: scalar GLSL-ish syntax over x and t, with the usual scalar builtins.

v.description: For a reference study, 'what the source does → what the lens does'. The arrow splits the cell into its two halves.

entry.description: An entry supplies its content EITHER inline here OR — the normal case — from content/<id>/entry.js, which the shell injects as a classic script and which calls Shell.registerEntry with this same shape. Registered fields win over inline ones of the same name.

id.description: Also the URL segment: #/<id>. Unique within the tool.

index.description: Display index shown in the rail ("11", "B1"). Editorial; NOT the sort key.

order.description: The sort key. Sparse, so an entry can be inserted without renumbering.

lane.description: Overrides the tool's default lane for this entry.

path.description: The entry folder. MUST NOT be named dist/, _site/ or node_modules/ — scripts/build-site.mjs filters those basenames out of the deploy copy at any depth. Defaults to content/<id>/.

text.description: Prose, as an HTML string. There is no fetch, so a prose FILE would need a second transport; a template literal next to the code it explains is the right authoring unit anyway.

fragment.description: fragment lane: the standalone HTML document for this lens.

stub.description: A flag, not a status: an entry can be canonical AND unfinished. Rendered as a mark beside the status.

designWidth.description: The width the fragment was composed at. The entry view shows it at this width and the page scrolls; contact-sheet previews render at this width and are CSS-scaled. Reflowing a lens into a 240px card is a different composition, not a thumbnail.

height.description: auto asks the fragment for its height over postMessage (fragment-boot.js). Nothing ever reads contentDocument.

texture.description: This chapter needs a source image (was `tex:true` in the old LESSONS array).

reference.description: The promoted REFERENCE STUDY table. Explicitly null means 'no decomposition on file' and the page says so out loud — a missing decomposition should be visible, not blank.

pass0.description: PASS 0 — DECOMPOSITION, promoted out of a CSS comment into data. Conventionally substrate / process / type / hardware / skeleton.

critique.description: Required in full on any entry presented as a canonical worked example: build-site.mjs fails the deploy on a canonical entry with a critique block that lacks reads_as, coupling or pass_order. It is a gate made of a JSON field, which is the cheapest kind.

coupling.description: PLAN §2.7: what drives what. The test that does the most work in the framework and had nowhere to live.

pass_order.description: PLAN §2.7: the order of operations, and why a different order is a different picture.

faults.description: FAULTS (pre-refine), promoted out of a CSS comment. Rendered behind the hatched rule — the one ornamental mark in the system, which earns its place by marking the one block that is an admission.

ruling.description: A dated, attributed decision — e.g. Ki-Landscapes/index.html:252, '// crisp edge (solid to 94%) — CANON, do not soften (julia 2026-06-10)'. The editorial layer these tools have never had; it belongs in data, not in a comment.

by.description: The person who made the decision, or the reserved value "proposed" for a ruling written here that is not yet hers. A ruling attributed to a person must be checkable: it carries a date, or a `source` naming the file and line its comment lives at, or both. build-site.mjs fails the deploy on an attributed ruling with neither.

source.description: file:line of the comment this ruling was promoted out of, e.g. "Ki-Landscapes/index.html:120-121". Added at checkpoint 8: two of the rulings that DO trace to Julia's own comments carry no date in the source, because the comment does not have one, and inventing a date would be worse than citing the line.

entity.description: What KIND of thing this record is. Defaults to `exploration` when omitted, which is what every currently-shipped lens or chapter is at ck-e0. A `technique` supplies a lesson and lists its instances; an `atom` carries `kind`, `params[]`, an engine file and a rendered swatch; a `style` is declared in the manifest's styles[] block (not here) and this value is used only for the six style landing entries; a `coupling` is an exploration with a `driver` + `consequences[]`.

kind.description: Required when entity=atom. The eleven-kind list from DOMAIN-MODEL §1.2.

uses.description: The atoms this entity is made of. Each item is an atom id, optionally with the parameters this instance chose — `{atom: 'paper-tooth', params: {tile: 180, blend: 'soft-light'}}`. build-site.mjs fails the deploy on an unresolvable atom id. This is the ladder: an exploration --uses--> atom <--produces-- technique is one join.

instance_of.description: The technique stack of this exploration, ORDERED. The order is the content — see the `critique.pass_order` field, which reads the same list in prose. build-site.mjs fails the deploy on an id that does not resolve to a technique in this manifest.

produces.description: Required on a technique whose lesson has been reified into an atom (paper tooth, dot screen, Freeverb). Declared here; the atom page shows the reverse link automatically at ck-e3.

governed_by.description: The skill ids that produce, critique or govern this entity. Every one must resolve against manifest.skills[]. All 14 are tagged; only competency rungs render pages (an unbuilt rung is deliberately empty).

driver.description: Coupling entries only. One sentence naming the single shared cause that fans out into `consequences[]`. See REVIEW-SOUND §2.2 — a coupling is NOT a third page-kind, it is an ordinary entry that declares a driver plus a consequences table.

consequences.description: Coupling entries only. Rows of [consequence, mapping, source-citation]. The audio adapter's proto renders exactly this. `#/couplings` becomes a saved query over entries that carry this field.

mute_test.description: Coupling entries only. The removal test aimed across the medium boundary — mute it, does the picture still read? freeze it, does the sound still make sense?

headroom.description: Audio entries only. Where the level decision lives in the graph, measured at the master output. Added at ck-e0 as the sixth test (REVIEW-SOUND §2.3).
